traits.fruit_surface.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 167, Cochemiea: fruit globose, naked, with a large terminal scar; Mammillaria (pp. 404 to 405), where Anderson keeps C. grahamii: pericarpel naked, berry naked.

traits.tubercle_relief.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 404 to 405, Cochemiea: tubercles distinct, spirally arranged, without grooves.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 4, 1923, p. 65), as Neomammillaria, the mammillarias, among which today's broad Cochemiea (the hook-spined mammillarias) stands: stems globose to short-cylindric, their tubercles in spiral rows, never on ribs, each tipped with its spine cluster.
